transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Noah (CSM), Maya (Aurelia CTO), Liam (Platform Eng), Priya (ML Infra)

Summary:
Quick sync on results from the priority-routing seqlen sweep, TTFT microburst behavior, and kernel experiment outcomes. Decide next steps for staging smoke and deliverables for next week.

Topics:
- TTFT vs streaming handoff
- Sequence length distribution and 99th percentile impact
- Kernel selection: fused-mha vs tiled kernels for short vs long seqs
- Hedged routing / priority lanes and cost tradeoffs
- Next steps: benches, logs, pricing

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: okay everybody uh thanks for carving out time. we wanted to run through the seqlen sweep results and the routing experiments. Evan, can you kick us off with a quick summary of the bench runs?
[00:22] Evan: yeah sure. so we ran three kernel profiles across the staged model builds -- baseline fused-mha optimized for 4-64 tokens, a tiled kernel that's better past 512, and a hybrid that switches at 128. we instrumented TTFT, steady-state tokens/second, and also microburst latency samples.
[00:38] Evan: quick note, the fused profile gave best TTFT for short responses, median around 18-22ms first byte, but the hybrid had smaller variance at the 95/99 tail during microbursts. there was a weird spike in one run where the NV PCI bus queued and then you see a 200ms tail, might be noise.
[01:02] Liam: sorry just to clarify, when you say TTFT are you measuring from request ingress or after our gateway TLS handshake? because our staging shows an extra 8-12ms there.
[01:12] Evan: good call, we're measuring at the Redwood agent boundary, after TLS - so it should include handshake. but i think some of your gateway instrumentation is adding extra TTF.
[01:23] Maya: um, we care about user-perceived first byte, so include the whole chain. if the edge is adding 10ms we need to account for that.
[01:33] Sofia: right. the point of the priority routing experiment is to move critical paths to the fast lane and ensure the trimmed kernel profile stays warm. Priya, did you pull the seqlen histogram?
[01:44] Priya: yes — last 30 days: median 36 tokens, 90th at 122, 95th 210, 99th 844. interestingly the 99.9th is near 4k which corresponds to a specific account/flow we saw.
[01:58] Priya: so if we set the hybrid switch at 128 we capture 92-93% of traffic in the low-latency path, which is nice.
[02:08] Evan: that aligns with our bench: hybrid kept TTFT near fused for small seqs but gave better tail. single downside is the cost bump when longer requests hit the tiled kernel but that's expected.
[02:21] Noah: do we have numbers on cost per 1k tokens for hybrid vs fused? customer wants delta for budgeting.
[02:29] Sofia: we'll include the pricing delta in the follow-up. quick question on hedging: during microbursts, did you try duplicating the request on a lower-cost pool as fallback, or just priority routing?
[02:41] Evan: we tested hedged duplicates at 50ms and 100ms delays. duplicate to a cheaper machine reduced 99th tail by ~60% but increased token cost by around 12% in our sim. also some crosstalk on KV cache warming when duplicate hits different hosts.
[03:00] Liam: that cache warm-up sounds important — our workloads rely on prefix caching for multi-turn. if duplicates invalidate or bypass kv cache we may get worse overall latency.
[03:10] Priya: yep, on multi-turn flows the KV cache hit rate dropped 7% in duplicates scenario. that partly explains the token cost bump because you end up regenerating some prefix passes.
[03:22] Maya: what's the simplest low-risk thing we can do in staging to prove improvement without blowing budget?
[03:27] Sofia: two low-risk options: A) priority lanes with hybrid kernel switch at 128 and warmed pool (no hedging), or B) small hedged duplicate only for routes tagged critical with 50ms hedging to a warmed pool. A is cheaper, B buys tail reduction at cost.
[03:44] Liam: i'd prefer A to start. we can enable request tagging for critical routes - less intrusive. then if tail persists we can toggle B for specific customers.
[03:52] Evan: operationally A needs a warmed warm lane with cache affinity; we can recommend pool pinning and pre-warming heuristics. B needs more orchestration and logging.
[04:02] Priya: and for A we'll need to set the hybrid switch threshold correctly; 128 seems right from the histogram but curious about the 95/99 effects if we shift to 256.
[04:12] Evan: shifting to 256 captures more traffic but increases average cost slightly and may degrade TTFT for mid-length requests. our bench shows TTFT median moves from 20ms to 25ms if you push switch to 256.
[04:24] Maya: show me the 99th for both thresholds — that's what exec will ask.
[04:29] Evan: yes i'll export that table. i have a csv with per-kernel 50/90/95/99 for thresholds 64/128/256.
[04:35] Sofia: great. can you also include microburst samples per run so they can see event correlation?
[04:40] Evan: will do.
[04:42] [05:00] Sofia: quick note on instrumentation: Liam, we asked you to turn on request-tag headers so Redwood can route by "priority:high". is that on your side yet?
[05:07] Liam: i'm on it, i'll flip it in staging today. i need the header spec.
[05:11] Sofia: we sent the spec in the doc earlier; i'll re-share. it's a simple x-rw-priority: high|normal|low header.
[05:18] Liam: perfect.
[05:20] [07:05] Evan: small gotcha — in our first hybrid run there was an artefact where tiled kernel produced slightly different tokenization around punctuation on one model variant, causing small degen differences. it's probably a model/compile mismatch.
[07:24]Priya: does that affect safety or outputs?
[07:27] Evan: negligible but worth noting — we'll pin model build and re-run.
[07:32]Maya: ok. about privacy/compliance: if we do hedging, duplicates might cross different physical hosts. we need to ensure no re-routing to non-compliant regions.
[07:41] Sofia: yes Redwood supports region pinning and we can ensure duplicates stay within the same compliance zone. we'll detail that in the follow-up.
[07:50] Noah: also to call out SSO/audit asks — Maya mentioned audit log retention. we can give an add-on for longer retention if you need it.
[07:58] Maya: thanks, we'll review cost.
[08:02] [11:40] Sofia: moving to final decisions — agreed: start with priority lanes + hybrid switch at 128, no hedging in initial smoke. Redwood to deliver kernels + csv and price delta. Aurelia to enable request tagging and run 48-hour smoke.
[11:56] Priya: we'll also generate sequence-length histogram and confirm the 99th cutpoint in our logs and share it.
[12:03] Evan: and i'll include the hedging sim numbers in case you want to toggle later.
[12:10] Liam: one ops question — how do we detect microburst vs normal variance? do we have a threshold?
[12:17] Evan: we use a sliding 1m window and mark events where 99th increases by >40% relative to baseline as microbursts; we can share the alert rules.
[12:26] Sofia: action items recap: Evan bench export, Sofia pricing + header spec, Liam enable tags + logs, Priya seq hist. schedule follow-up mid-next-week.
[12:38] Maya: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[12:41] Sofia: thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite.

References/Links mentioned:
- seqlen_histogram.csv (will be shared)
- kernel_bench_results.csv (Evan)
- priority-routing-spec.md (Sofia)

End of transcript.
